title: Edmunds and Dodgers’ Tommy ‘Tanks’ Edman Fuel LA Fans with $25,000 Gas Giveaway on Sept. 25
author: Edmunds
body:
SANTA MONICA, Calif., Sept. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Los Angeles-based car shopping site Edmunds today announced it is fueling Los Angeles Dodgers fans for October baseball with $25,000 in free gas on Friday, September 25.
Edmunds is joining forces with Dodgers fan-favorite #25 Tommy ‘Tanks’ Edman for the Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway at Longo Lexus in El Monte, CA. Fans must arrive by car to participate and are encouraged to wear Dodger blue attire. A total of 333 $75 gas gift cards from 76® will be distributed while supplies last, limited to one per vehicle.
With Edman and the team away for their final regular season series in San Francisco, Dodgers fans are invited to root on the Boys in Blue as they gear up for October baseball.
Taking ‘Tommy Tanks’ Beyond the Ballpark with $25K in Free Gas
Playing off Edman’s No. 25, Edmunds will give away $25,000 in gas on September 25, bringing his ‘Tommy Tanks’ moniker beyond the ballpark and to the pump for LA drivers.
- Date: Friday, September 25
- Time: 6 - 8 PM
- Location: Longo Lexus in El Monte, CA (3530 Peck Rd, El Monte, CA 91731)
- How to Participate: Fans must arrive by car and enter Longo Lexus through the main entrance on Peck Road; walk-up entry is not permitted. One person per vehicle will receive a wristband before parking and heading to the Longo Lexus showroom to complete a quick form, engage with the Tommy Tanks Gas Calculator, and receive the gift card. Dodgers gear is encouraged! A total of 333 $75 gas gift cards from 76® will be available while supplies last, limited to one per vehicle.
- More Information: Full event details and giveaway rules can be found at edmunds.com/freegas.
VIDEO: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/r6zzAd3Iqtk
Dodgers Fans Said They’d Turn Down $1 Gas for Another Championship. Edmunds is Fueling Their Dedication.
The Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway was inspired by a survey of more than 2,000 Dodgers fans conducted by Edmunds earlier this season1 that revealed just how far fans are willing to go for the Boys in Blue. When asked to choose between the Dodgers winning a third consecutive World Championship or gas prices falling to $1 per gallon, 80% chose another ring. And they’re willing to brave some serious LA traffic for their team, too: Nearly one-third (32%) said they’d spend five hours or more traveling to and from a Dodgers home game in October.
“Between driving in LA traffic and keeping up with high fuel costs, local drivers could use a win,” said Tommy Edman. “Teaming with Edmunds to fuel up the best fanbase in baseball for another October run is an awesome way to thank LA for showing up for us night in and night out.”
High Gas Prices Add to Affordability Pressures for LA Drivers 
The giveaway comes as LA drivers continue to face stubbornly high prices at the pump, adding to the persistent affordability challenges facing vehicle owners. According to AAA, the average price for regular fuel in the Los Angeles/Long Beach metro area was $6.09 yesterday, September 16. 
The pressure at the pump comes as consumers are already navigating record-high vehicle expenses: Edmunds recently reported that the average monthly payment on new-vehicle purchases hit a new record of $777 in Q2, and the average price for a 3-year-old used vehicle rose to $32,461 last quarter, a new second-quarter record.
“We know how much Southern Californians rely on their cars and how quickly the costs of driving can add up,” said Alison Steinlauf Anziska, senior vice president of marketing at Edmunds. “Dodgers fans have shown us just how far they’ll go to support their team, and Tommy’s been showing them exactly why they call him ‘Tommy Tanks.’ We thought it would be fun to take that nickname beyond the ballpark and give fans a little relief at the pump as they cheer on the Dodgers into October.”
More Dodgers Fan Survey Findings Highlight Serious Dedication
Beyond their willingness to choose another Dodgers championship over $1 gas and spend long hours on the road traveling to October home games, Edmunds’ survey of more than 2,000 Dodgers fans from earlier this season revealed a few other ways their fandom shows up on and off the road:
- Many fans are susceptible to catching a case of the ‘Dodger blues’: Two-thirds (66%) of fans said they have skipped work, school or another major obligation to attend a Dodger game.
- Dodgers passion extends to the driveway: 13% of Dodger fans drive a blue car, well above the California state average of 7% of new vehicles sold in 2025.
- Fuel economy matters to Dodgers fans: When considering the car-shopping priorities that mattered most to fans, fuel economy ranked among the top three factors, along with price and reliability.
Edmunds, Edman and the Dodgers Go ‘Back-to-Back’
The gas giveaway and fan survey are the latest elements of Edmunds’ ‘Back to Back’ brand campaign in collaboration with the Dodgers and Edman. As part of the campaign, Edmunds is also transforming its Gas Savings Calculator into the ‘Tommy Tanks Gas Calculator,’ helping consumers estimate how much they could save on fuel by switching to a more fuel-efficient vehicle or different powertrain.
Earlier this season, Edmunds executed a sweepstakes offering fans a chance at the ultimate VIP gameday experience and a free vehicle appraisal. Edmunds also launched ‘The Challenge,’ the brand’s second consecutive hero digital ad campaign starring Edman as he helps fans make the right call in their next car shopping decision with the help of Edmunds.
For more information and official rules, check out the Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway event page at edmunds.com/freegas.
1 *Source: Edmunds survey of Dodgers fans, n=2,071, April 2026
About Longo Lexus
Longo Lexus, located in El Monte, California, is a premier Lexus dealership dedicated to delivering exceptional guest experiences throughout every stage of the vehicle ownership journey. Part of Penske Motor Group, Longo Lexus has been recognized as the #1 Lexus dealership for new vehicle sales in the Western United States since opening in 1990. The dealership offers an extensive selection of new, L/Certified, and pre-owned vehicles, supported by state-of-the-art service, parts, collision repair, and in-house customization facilities. Built on a longstanding commitment to integrity, excellence, and putting guests first, Longo Lexus continues to set the standard for luxury automotive retail and ownership. For more information, visit longolexus.com or follow Longo Lexus on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and LinkedIn. 
About Edmunds
Edmunds guides car shoppers online from research to purchase. With in-depth reviews of every new vehicle, shopping tips from an in-house team of experts, plus a wealth of consumer and automotive market insights, Edmunds helps millions of shoppers each month select, price and buy a car with confidence. Regarded as one of America's best workplaces by Newsweek, Fortune, Great Place to Work and Built In, Edmunds is based in Santa Monica, California. Follow us on TikTok, Twitter, Facebook and Instagram.

title: Blake Snell’s Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
author: TJ French
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers endured a bit of an injury scare regarding starter Blake Snell in their recent game against the Cincinnati Reds.
Snell, who made the start for LA, was pulled after just one inning with groin tightness.
During the game, reports surfaced that the Snell injury was not thought to be serious, and that Snell should still be in line to make his start.
Well, after the end of the game, Snell spoke with the media, and his comments about the injury should give Dodgers fans some assurance.
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
What Did Blake Snell Say About His Groin Injury?
Per @SportsNetLA, here is some of what Blake Snell had to say about his early exit:
"I was gonna try to get through five, but I just knew I didn't have a good shot of doing that and remaining healthy."
He also added that he's "day-to-day", and "should be good" to make his next start.
So while many Dodgers fans may have been panicking after he was pulled from the game, it's expected to be a precautionary measure.
The Dodgers' October rotation would still look very formidable without Blake Snell in it, but considering Snell's additions last October, LA is likely going to be as careful as possible when it comes to him being at a full bill of health in a few weeks.

title: Dave Roberts can't hide Dodgers' issues with Shohei Ohtani, Edwin Diaz updates
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may be back to their winning ways, but it's impossible for fans to ignore the fact that they've been playing sub-.500 teams since the beginning of September and only have one series against a winning team left on their schedule.
The rotation has been hit with another injury, the bullpen is still in bad shape, Shohei Ohtani is still injured and, maybe worst of all, Edwin Díaz is coming back.
Dave Roberts said ahead of the Dodgers' finale against the Cincinnati Reds that Díaz will be activated on Friday, but with the caveat that he'll only pitch in low leverage. Of Ohtani: "He's feeling normal...ish" but continues to progress. Neither are ringing endorsements.
Dodgers fans have been forced to wonder if any lead would be too big for Díaz to blow. He bounced back from a disastrous rehab appearance (⅔ innings, five earned runs) with a much more promising one (one scoreless), but the Díaz conundrum is one they're going to have to go back to the drawing board with in the offseason.
Ohtani is eligible to come off the IL next Wednesday and the Dodgers will want to give him a ramp-up before the postseason, but "normal...ish" is not an indication that they should.
Edwin Díaz set to return to Dodgers on Friday; Shohei Ohtani feeling "normal...ish"
The Dodgers are still trying to lock up a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves, who are only behind by 3.5 games, so they still can't just rest on their laurels after clinching the NL West. Using Díaz in any of the games ahead, even if it's a 10-plus run blowout, doesn't seem wise.
But they also can't just ignore their $69 million closer entirely. What we might see from the Dodgers is a soft ghosting — maybe Díaz will only get the ball in a favorable matchup to end an inning. Under no circumstances should he be allowed on LA's postseason roster.
When it comes to Ohtani, the situation gets even more sticky. He'll presumably take back his leadoff spot in the Dodgers' lineup when he returns, but if he looks anything like he did in his last game before going onto the IL, postseason opponents will be more than happy to take the easy out to start a game.
Don't let the Dodgers' postseason berth and clinching the NL West fool you: they're in some trouble. Their 2024 and 2025 postseason rosters all had their own weaknesses, but this year's might be the most jeopardized we've seen yet.

title: Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal takes part in Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s intense training routine
author: Chris Trant
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are entering the final stretch of the MLB regular season with their sights set on winning a third straight World Series title. Once again, the pitching staff has been a major reason they remain positioned for another postseason run.
Los Angeles entered Thursday's game against the Cincinnati Reds with a 92-60 record, three games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for first place in the National League.
Los Angeles already had one of baseball's top starters in Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the rotation became even more intimidating when the team acquired two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline.
Since Skubal's move to Los Angeles, he and Yamamoto have bolstered one of the most effective rotations in all of baseball.
Sharing Secrets
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) winds up in the second inning of the MLB National League game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Los Angeles Dodgers at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati on Monday, Sept. 14, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Skubal appears to be taking advantage of having another elite pitcher around him, even experimenting with one of Yamamoto's more unusual training methods. As seen in a video from Shinji Omiya of The Asahi Shimbun, a prominent Japanese newspaper, Yamamoto demonstrated a javelin-style throwing exercise for Skubal to try.
"Yoshinobu Yamamoto the pitcher was teaching the two-time consecutive Cy Young lefty Skubal how to throw the javelin. It traced a beautiful parabolic arc, and they were both smiling," Omiya shared on X.
Yamamoto has become known for an unconventional approach to warmups, and he frequently stands out from typical MLB training. Yamamoto originally adopted the javelin warm-up in order to relieve stress on his elbow while generating lower-body power.
Two Aces Rolling
The results suggest that both pitchers have found routines that work for them.
Coming off a season in which he won World Series MVP, Yamamoto has put together another stellar season. Starting 27 games, Yamamoto owns a 2.51 ERA, 0.87 WHIP and 178 strikeouts across 179 innings.
Skubal has been excellent as well in Los Angeles, starting eight games for the Dodgers and posting a 2.52 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 57 strikeouts in 50 innings.
Clearly, neither pitcher needs to reinvent his approach, but Dodger fans are likely pleased to see two of their elite arms sharing knowledge ahead of a potentially historic postseason run.

title: Tarik Skubal Embraces Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s Unusual Dodgers Training Method
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal was spotted doing Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s signature workout ahead of the team’s game vs. the Reds.
Skubal has been on the team for only a month or so, but he seems to be taking a liking to his fellow starters.
On Thursday, September 17th, Skubal was spotted with Yamamoto and his translator, throwing the javelin, a staple of the Japanese star.
Yamamoto has been one of the more unique minds when it comes to his preparation, using a ton of flexibility and motion techniques.
This is not the first sign of Skubal’s appreciation for Yamamoto. When he first joined the team, Skubal was impressed with Yamamoto right off the bat.
“Yoshi’s process is nuts too, you know. I think that what he does is insane too, and watching his bullpens, the preparation is second to none,” Skubal told Dodgers Nation.
Why does Yamamoto throw javelins?
His famous javelin toss is just one part of a routine created by personal trainer Osamu Yada, who started working with Yamamoto during his teenage years in Japan.
Since then, “Yada Sensei,” as he is referred to, has worked with other members of the Dodgers, including Mookie Betts over the spring.
“I’m not fully in his whole routine,” Betts said of Yada. “But I wake up every morning and do my stretch routine that Sensei showed me, throwing the javelins every day.
“I think throwing javelins is the reason why I can make a play in the hole like that and throw it in the air on a line. I’m really grateful for Yoshi and Sensei, because they have definitely changed my perspective, changed my life, changed my game.”
Yamamoto has credited these workouts as the main reason the Dodgers’ ace can pitch often and, thus far, avoid serious injuries.
If the javelin can help Skubal as well, Yada Sensei’s legend will only grow.

title: Dave Roberts' Shohei Ohtani Update Is Not Exactly Inspiring
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
For much of the season, Shohei Ohtani was the MVP frontrunner, but things have changed in a hurry.
He has not pitched since the All-Star break, after being stellar on the mound through his 14 starts. He has been dealing with knee and biceps injuries, but his offense was still great until it wasn't. Ohtani's injuries started impacting his play at the plate, and the Dodgers tried to manage it with off days before putting him on the injured list.
Ohtani is eligible to return from the injured list before the regular season ends, and the Dodgers anticipate that he will be ready to go when the time comes. However, whether the time off actually allowed him to get back to 100% is unknown.
"Feels normal…ish," manager Dave Roberts said of Ohtani, who started up activity on Tuesday, per The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Ohtani did not report any discomfort after starting up baseball activities again, which is good, but his injuries may simply be something he has to manage the rest of the way. However, the Dodgers are hoping that the time on the injured list at least gets him to a point where he can manage things and be productive.
Since Aug. 8, when he started a throwing progression to try and get back in the rotation, Ohtani is slashing .198/.294/.396 with just four home runs. He did not complain about the injuries impacting his swing until the Dodgers until a four-strikeout game on Sept. 2. The Dodgers are hoping the extended time off will get him back on track.

title: Edwin Díaz rejoining Dodgers with last chance to salvage disastrous season in new role
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– Edwin Díaz is set to be activated by the Dodgers on Friday, manager Dave Roberts announced.
It leaves the $69 million offseason signing with plenty to prove over the final week of the regular season.
After beginning the year as a marquee free-agent acquisition seen as one of the best closers in all the major leagues, Díaz’s first season in Los Angeles has been an injury-plagued, performance-hampered disaster.
He has made only 16 appearances. He has converted only seven of his 11 save opportunities. He has posted an unthinkable 11.85 ERA while dealing with a litany of physical ailments.
First, there were loose bodies in his elbow that required a surgical procedure in April. Then, after returning in late July, he went down again with neck inflammation just three weeks later. At other points, he complained of discomfort in his previously surgically repaired right knee. Put it all together, he has never looked right with his mechanics or delivery.
The Dodgers were hopeful Díaz’s latest IL stint would give him time to remedy those issues. They identified a drop in his arm slot as a potential root cause for his lack of consistency this year.
But then, in his first four rehab outings with Triple-A Oklahoma City earlier this month, he gave up six runs (including five in one appearance) and walked seven batters, prompting Roberts earlier this week to cast doubt on Díaz’s chances of making the postseason roster.
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts said. “It hasn’t been good.”

title: Dodgers news: Will Shohei Ohtani return from injury before MLB playoffs? Here's the latest update
author: Zachary Draves; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Will Shohei Ohtani return from injury before MLB playoffs? Here's the latest update appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are vying for their third consecutive World Series title. And of course, everyone is wondering about Shohei Ohtani.
He has been battling a series of injuries, including knee inflammation, bicep tightness, and neck strain.
On Thursday, manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani has been making progress, per Jack Harris of The California Post. He said that Ohtani will be making his way back to coach pitching.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Meanwhile, Roberts said that Ohtani is feeling "normalish," per Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
The Dodgers clinched their 14th straight playoff berth and are on track to win yet another National League West Division title. Los Angeles is a heavy favorite going into the postseason.
But for Ohtani, it's been an up-and-down year, especially on the mound.
Altogether, he has pitched in 14 games, posting an 8-2 record, a 1.79 ERA, and 95 strikeouts. However, injuries have kept Ohtani out of the starting rotation.
That has jeopardized his chances of winning another NL MVP Award. An honor that will likely go to Chicago Cubs CF Pete Crow-Armstrong. The contest between the two for the honor has captivated the baseball world in the later half of the season.
Nevertheless, Ohtani has remained solid at the plate, even as his numbers declined. He is batting .277 with 139 hits, 30 home runs, and 80 RBIs.
In his NL MVP season last year, Ohtani batted .282 with 172 hits, 55 home runs, and 102 RBIs.
The Dodgers will wrap up a road series against the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday. Afterward, they will begin a home series against the San Francisco Giants.

Related: Dodgers promote pitcher after making Bobby Miller roster move

title: Dave Roberts: First-round bye would be more ‘beneficial’ than ever for injury-riddled Dodgers
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now.
“I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason.
Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch that first-round bye. The Dodgers trail the Milwaukee Brewers by three games for the top seed.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset,” Roberts said. “But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge.”
Blake Snell joined the long list of players with injury concerns when he left his start Wednesday after just one inning due to left groin tightness. The Dodgers also have questions about Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps), Freddie Freeman (knee), Edgardo Henriquez (back), Andy Pages (hand), Roki Sasaki (blister) and Dalton Rushing (elbow).
Pages has been swinging a bat and hitting off the Trajekt machine this week, and it is “very likely” he will be activated from the IL during the homestand starting Friday, according to Roberts.
Ohtani has been “progressing” this week and is feeling “normal-ish” with no pain in his right arm or left knee, Roberts said.
“He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when (his) time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Snell could undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his groin injury. But he was optimistic after the game Wednesday that he had pulled back and left the game soon enough that it won’t be a serious issue and he might be able to make one more start before the end of the regular season.
“It’s all contingent on how he feels and potential imaging,” Roberts said. “It doesn’t make sense to just shut him down until the postseason if he can pitch. But again, if he’s not 100 percent to pitch, then we have no problem kicking the can.”
DIAZ RETURN
Right-hander Edwin Diaz completed his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday and will join the Dodgers in Los Angeles this weekend with the expectation that he will be activated from the Injured List.
Diaz will be used in “low-leverage” situations, Roberts said, with a need to prove he can pitch well enough to assume a bigger role if he is on the postseason roster.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Roberts called Diaz’s final outing with OKC was “his best one yet.” Diaz pitched a scoreless inning, gave up a double and didn’t get a single swing-and-miss on any of 15 pitches.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said of what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA), Friday, 7:10 p.m., Apple TV, 570 AM

title: Edwin “Sugar” Díaz será activado el viernes por los Dodgers
author: Por Redacción El Nuevo Día
body:
Edwin Díaz se unirá este viernes a los Dodgers en el inicio de una serie ante los Giants de San Francisco. (Nick Wass)
Por Redacción El Nuevo Día
El relevista puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz retornará con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles cuando la novena lo active de la lista de lesionados este viernes, confirmó el dirigente Dave Roberts.
El regreso de Díaz se producirá después de completar el miércoles una entrada sin permitir carreras en su quinta aparición de rehabilitación en Triple A con la novena de Oklahoma City.
“La idea es que esté activo el viernes”, expresó Roberts este jueves, según SportsNet LA.
El naguabeño trabajó la novena entrada y necesitó 15 lanzamientos, 11 de ellos para strikes. Permitió un doble con dos outs, pero evitó que el corredor anotara para completar el episodio en blanco.
Roberts calificó la actuación como la mejor de Díaz durante su asignación de rehabilitación.
Dodgers injury updates, per manager Roberts (via @ByJackHarris):
• Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from IL on Friday • Andy Pages (hand) "very likely" to be activated during final homestand • Shohei Ohtani (biceps) could still return before end of regular season
La salida resultaba particularmente importante para el boricua después de su difícil presentación del domingo, cuando permitió cinco carreras limpias, concedió tres bases por bolas y apenas consiguió dos outs.
De hecho, Roberts había reconocido el lunes que Díaz necesitaba lanzar mejor y que su presencia en el roster de los Dodgers para la postemporada no estaba garantizada.
El regreso tampoco significa que Díaz retomará inmediatamente las funciones de cerrador.
Roberts había adelantado que utilizará inicialmente al derecho de 32 años en situaciones de poca presión mientras intenta recuperar la confianza del cuerpo técnico.
Los Dodgers ya aseguraron su pase a los playoffs y marchan primeros en la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. El viernes inician una serie de tres juegos ante San Francisco.
Díaz está en la lista de lesionados desde el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Es su segunda ausencia prolongada de la temporada luego de que en abril fuera sometido a una operación para remover cuerpos sueltos de su codo derecho.
Díaz tiene marca de 2-2 y efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 18 carreras limpias permitidas en 13.2 entradas. Además, ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.

title: Dodgers' Edwin Diaz to return for series opener against Giants
author: Sportsnet Staff
body:
The closer will be active for Game 1 of the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday.
Roberts added that Diaz will pitch in low-leverage situations.
The 32-year-old right-hander signed a three-year, $60-million contract in the off-season to become the Dodgers' closer, but has struggled with injuries and underperformance.
Diaz underwent an arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right eblow in April and most recently missed time due to neck inflammation. He has an 11.85 ERA with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13.2 innings.
Roberts also said that the Dodgers plan to activate outfielder Andy Pages on their upcoming homestand, and that Shohei Ohtani could still return this season.
The two-time reigning National League MVP tried to return from a nagging bicep injury on Sept. 7 but was placed on the 15-day injured list afterward. He will not pitch again this season.

title: Shohei Ohtani’s feeling ‘normal…ish’ as Dodgers sort out health issues before playoffs
author: Fabian Ardaya
body:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers have kept open the possibility that Shohei Ohtani will return before the end of the regular season, though they are up against a running clock.
Any progress is good progress for the Dodgers’ most important piece, so it was a good thing when Ohtani started up activity Tuesday and Thursday and didn’t report any discomfort in his bothersome biceps, balky left knee and tight neck.
“Feels normal…ish,” manager Dave Roberts said Thursday morning.
Advertisement
Ohtani went on the injured list late last week, ending a months-long injury saga and giving him a maximum of five additional regular season games to play in before another the playoffs. He is eligible to return as soon as Sept. 23, though Roberts did not commit to that timeline.
There are still steps for Ohtani to take. He swung off a tee on Tuesday, had Wednesday off from baseball activity and could hit off a coach’s pitching by the end of the week. He will need to face some sort of live pitching before he appears in a game and even then, the maximum of five games does not feel like a lot for him to get his timing right.
Especially since, given how the Dodgers tried kicking the can on shelving Ohtani, he will return after having taken just four plate appearances since Sept. 2. Ohtani, clearly compromised by his nagging injuries, had just six hits over his final 49 at-bats before hitting the IL.
They still need Ohtani, even if he is not 100 percent. The oldest lineup in baseball has shown its age. Even if Ohtani’s role on the postseason roster is simply to provide the threat of launching a ball into the seats, that is valuable in their quest for a third consecutive World Series title. The Dodgers’ first road trip without Ohtani since his arrival in 2024 has been noticeably different.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yoshinobu Yamamoto joked through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. Yamamoto has instead had to rely on Roki Sasaki, “but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Díaz’ place in the bullpen
Edwin Díaz will return to the Dodgers on Friday, but not as the club’s closer. Nothing is guaranteed for the guy the Dodgers gave $69 million to solve their ninth-inning problem and who now could be on the bubble for the postseason roster thanks to his 11.85 ERA.
Díaz, who has made only 16 major-league appearances thanks to arthroscopic elbow surgery and a later neck issue, has also pitched poorly in rehab. A five-run blowup on Sunday with Triple-A Oklahoma City caused the Dodgers to delay Díaz’s return. But a scoreless inning on Wednesday — albeit one in which Díaz gave up a 104 mph double and did not induce a single swing-and-miss — was enough for the Dodgers to bring him back to the big leagues.
“It was his best one yet,” Roberts said of Díaz, whose has a low bar to clear.
Advertisement
Díaz will return in lower-leverage situations and have to show prove over the final week of the regular season he deserves a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen, even if their list of right-handed relief options is thinning.
“I think like anything it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities but then you also got to perform, right?”
Edgardo Henriquez was the club’s most trusted reliever before he went on the injured list on Monday. Subsequent imaging showed what Roberts dubbed a “low-grade” back strain, and the manager said he was “hopeful” that Henriquez could still be a postseason option.
Another potential solution, Sasaki, is now needed in the rotation after Blake Snell exited Wednesday’s start with left groin tightness. The Dodgers will know more about Snell’s fate once they return to Los Angeles and potentially get imaging done, but Sasaki is currently slated to pitch at some point next week against the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers have also been cagey about Tyler Glasnow’s status. Roberts was vague after Glasnow’s last start, but said the right-hander “didn’t feel great” going into it. The Dodgers sent Glasnow directly to Los Angeles afterwards rather than have him travel with the club to Cincinnati, and Roberts said Glasnow’s preparation for Friday’s start has otherwise been normal.
Pages’ return imminent
Andy Pages will “very likely” return to the Dodgers’ lineup without playing in rehab games at some point during the six-game home stand that opens Friday. Pages has progressed quickly from left hand fracture and the Dodgers are banking on the All-Star’s defensive value in center field despite the chances he’ll struggle on offensive.
Pages moved from hitting softer baseballs to hitting normal ones this week and will hit off the Trajekt Arc machine to simulate live at-bats. There aren’t a lot of games to go around on a rehab assignment, anyway, though Oklahoma City did clinch a postseason berth on Wednesday (those games start next week).

title: Dodgers latest injury crisis throws Roki Sasaki usage plan in flux
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– Even after watching Roki Sasaki complete the final checkmark in his recovery from a blister on Wednesday afternoon, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts couldn’t say for sure how the team would use the 24-year-old phenom pitcher.
All year, it seemed clear that Sasaki was destined to wind up back in the Dodgers bullpen, reprising the late-inning leverage role he unexpectedly ascended to as a rookie last October.
Though he had turned a corner as a starter during the second half of this campaign, posting a 2.31 ERA in his first six outings after the All-Star break, he had still long looked like a superfluous piece of the Dodgers’ rotation, an excess arm stuck behind the four veteran superstars the club had penciled in to lead this fall’s World Series push.
However, Roberts remained non-committal about Sasaki’s plan on Wednesday, after the right-hander completed a four-inning, 48-pitch session of live batting practice in Cincinnati, in what was hoped to be his final step before returning from the injured list.
On the one hand, the skipper noted, the Dodgers could shift Sasaki to the bullpen now, give him time to re-acclimate to relief duties, and let him focus on just short-burst stints.
But on the other, “one can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts countered. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Hours later, the something Roberts was worried about might have suddenly happened –– with Blake Snell’s groin injury having direct repercussions on Sasaki’s potential task.
In Wednesday night’s game, Snell left his start after just one inning because of left groin tightness. While he’s hopeful he avoided any serious injury, he has had bouts of groin issues in the past that have sidelined him for up to a month at a time.
If that were to be the case again now, Sasaki would be first in line to replace Snell in the Dodgers’ postseason rotation.
Mix in the uncertainty surrounding fellow starter Tyler Glasnow faced following his four-inning outing last weekend in Miami –– after which he conspicuously returned immediately to Los Angeles to limit extra travel on the rest of this road trip –– and Sasaki now seems like a valuable starting-pitching insurance policy the Dodgers might still need to utilize in the playoffs.
That’s why, by the end of Wednesday’s game, Roberts was able to at least be definitive about the team’s plan for Sasaki when he comes off the injured list, confirming he is likely to make a start sometime next week, perhaps during a visit from the San Diego Padres.
In a best-case scenario, that will be Sasaki’s last time starting a game this year, with an otherwise healthy rotation allowing the Dodgers to shift him to an equally banged-up bullpen.
But for now, the team can’t be certain of anything.
Which means, when it comes to Sasaki, all options remain on the table.

title: This day in Dodgers history: Hideo Nomo, Sandy Koufax and more
author: Blake Williams
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a long line of notable pitchers and on this day in franchise history, those stars shined a little brighter throughout the years.
On Sept. 17, 1963, Sandy Koufax pitched a shutout against the St. Louis Cardinals at Sportsman’s Park while giving up just four hits.
The shutout was his 11th of the season, which set a new National League record for the most in one year by a left-hander in MLB history. Grover Cleveland Alexander held the Major League Record with 16 shutouts during the 1916 season for the Philadelphia Phillies.
Also on this day in Dodgers history but during the 1981 season, Fernando Valenzuela threw his eighth shutout of the year with a three-hitter against the Atlanta Braves.
With eight shutouts, Valenzuela tied the rookie record that was set by Chicago White Sox pitcher Ewell Russell in 1913. In addition, Valenzuela broke the previous NL mark shared by Irving Young (Boston Beaneaters, 1905), Grover Cleveland Alexander (Phillies, 1911), and Jerry Koosman (New York Mets, 1968).
Dodgers history: Sept. 17
Nomo no-hitter
In 1996, 15 years after Valenzuela and 33 years after Koufax set their shutout records, Hideo Nomo threw the only no-hitter in history at Coors Field. It was one of two Nomo tossed during his 12-year career.
Nomo’s historic game came with the club locked in a pennant race and it was the 20th no-hitter in franchise history.
Joe Torre retires
Also on this day in Dodgers history, manager Joe Torre announced he will retire following the end of the 2010 season. He finished his career with a record of 2326-1997 (.538) during his 30 seasons as a skipper with Mets, Braves, Cardinals, New York Yankees, and the Dodgers.
The Dodgers then announced the team’s hitting coach Don Mattingly was hired to replace Torre, who accepted a position to assist Major League Baseball Commissioner Bud Selig as the new Executive Vice President for Baseball Operations.

In 1996, 15 years after Valenzuela and 33 years after Koufax set their shutout records, Hideo Nomo threw the only no-hitter in history at Coors Field. It was one of two Nomo tossed during his 12-year career.
Nomo’s historic game came with the club locked in a pennant race and it was the 20th no-hitter in franchise history.
Joe Torre retires
Also on this day in Dodgers history, manager Joe Torre announced he will retire following the end of the 2010 season. He finished his career with a record of 2326-1997 (.538) during his 30 seasons as a skipper with Mets, Braves, Cardinals, New York Yankees, and the Dodgers.
The Dodgers then announced the team’s hitting coach Don Mattingly was hired to replace Torre, who accepted a position to assist Major League Baseball Commissioner Bud Selig as the new Executive Vice President for Baseball Operations.
Make sure to follow Dodger Blue on Instagram! It’s the best way to see exclusive coverage from games and events, get your questions answered, and more!

title: Dodgers To Make Edwin Diaz Earn High Leverage Appearances Again
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are expected to activate Edwin Díaz from the injured list on Friday, but he will not slot back into closing games right away.
According to the Orange County Register's Bill Plunkett, Dave Roberts said the plan is to activate Díaz for the San Francisco Giants series, but to have him pitch in "low leverage" situations for the time being. Roberts also called the bullpen a "meritocracy" and said that Díaz needs to prove himself.
Díaz was the National League Reliever of the Year last year and has won three career Reliever of the Year Awards. The Dodgers gave him a three-year, $69 million deal in the offseason, but he has had a terrible season.
Through his first six games, he had a 10.50 ERA and blew a save. He then underwent a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow. After returning, he posted a 12.91 ERA in nine games, blowing three saves. The Dodgers placed him on the injured list with neck inflammation on Aug. 18 and are hoping for the best version of him this time.
Díaz has noted that he thinks fixing his arm angle will help him, but it's a results-based business. He will have to prove he can pitch like the Dodgers expected him to be, and the Dodgers need him more now than ever.
Since the All-Star Break, the Dodgers bullpen has a 4.34 ERA, ranked 20th in baseball. The bullpen also has a 10.4% walk rate, the seventh-worst in baseball. Dodgers relievers have also given up 24 home runs in the second half. If Díaz can come back and pitch like an All-Star, it will go a long way in fixing the bullpen woes. The team is currently without Edgardo Henriquez, so they need a reliable right-hander in the bullpen.
Roberts also confirmed that outfielder Andy Pages (hand) is expected to rejoin LA during upcoming homestand without requiring a minor-league rehab assignment.
More MLB: Los Angeles Dodgers Reveal When Andy Pages Will Make Return

title: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani: Taking swings off coaches
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Thursday that Ohtani (biceps/knee) has progressed to hitting off coaches, Jack Harris of the California Post reports.
Ohtani has been easing back into a hitting progression after landing on the 15-day injured list last week with biceps and knee injuries. He is eligible for activation Sept. 23, and he could be back on that date or shortly after to get a few regular season games under his belt before the playoffs.

title: Andy Pages "Very Likely" to Be Activated During Upcoming Dodgers Homestand - MLB News | Fantasy Baseball
author: Will Brady
body:
Sep 17, 2026, 11:27 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it's "very likely" that outfielder Andy Pages (hand) will be activated during the team's upcoming homestand, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Los Angeles begins a six-game homestand on Friday. Pages has been sidelined since August 21 by a fractured left hand, but it appears he is now on the doorstep of a return to the big leagues. Across 550 plate appearances before the injury, the 25-year-old hit .272/.338/.458 with 21 home runs, 80 RBI, 72 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases. Pages was the Dodgers' everyday center fielder before getting hurt and should resume that role upon his return. Once activated, Pages profiles as a must-start outfielder for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris
More Recent News
Sep 17, 2026, 11:34 AM ET
Across 470 plate appearances in 2026, Chicago White Sox outfielder Tristan Peters is hitting .273/.343/.452 with 12 home runs, 54 RBI, 61 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. The lefty-swinger is hitting .192 across just 63 plate appearances against left-handed pitching, so his big-side platoon role limits his fantasy value to some degree. However, Peters owns an .824 OPS against right-handers and brings a balanced profile at the plate that allows him to provide modest production across all five fantasy categories. After hitting six home runs across 87 plate appearances in August, the 26-year-old has gone without a homer in his first 56 trips to the plate in September. Still, Peters hits for average and should continue to provide steady run production in stretches where the White Sox face a string of right-handed starting pitchers. Heading into the final week-plus of the regular season, Peters could be worth targeting as an outfield streamer off the waiver wire.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Edwin Diaz Set to Be Activated on Friday
                        
                            
                                Will Brady
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 17, 2026, 11:19 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said that right-hander Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from the 15-day injured list on Friday, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Diaz has struggled on his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he's made five appearances. However, the 32-year-old pitched a scoreless inning on Wednesday and is now on his way back to the big leagues. It's been a lost season for Diaz, who has missed extensive time due to elbow and neck issues. He's also been awful when healthy, pitching to an 11.85 ERA with a 2.56 WHIP across 13 2/3 innings in his first season with the Dodgers. It's unclear whether he'll assume the Dodgers' closer role immediately upon his return, or if he will need to prove that he's regained his form first. Dodgers left-hander Tanner Scott has largely been effective in Diaz's absence, logging a 2.87 ERA and 22 saves across 59 2/3 innings.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris
Sep 17, 2026, 11:12 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter/starting pitcher Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) is making progress and has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Ohtani is currently on the 15-day injured list as he battles lingering knee and biceps issues. The Dodgers have already announced that Ohtani will not pitch again this season, but the 32-year-old is expected to resume his role as the team's everyday designated hitter. Across 596 plate appearances in 2026, Ohtani is hitting .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 89 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. His production had begun to trail off before he was placed on the IL, with just one hit in 14 plate appearances in September. Still, Ohtani has the potential to swing fantasy leagues if he can return for the final weekend of the regular season.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris
MacKenzie Gore Dealing With "Muscle Spasms" in Back/Shoulder
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 17, 2026, 12:10 AM ET
Texas Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said that left-hander MacKenzie Gore (back, shoulder) had "muscle spasms" in his back/shoulder area during his start on Wednesday in the 7-3 win over the visiting Boston Red Sox, according to Shawn McFarland of The Dallas Morning News. Gore was given a no-decision at Globe Life Field, allowing three earned runs on two hits (one homer) while walking three and striking out none in four innings of work. The 27-year-old southpaw is now up in the air for his next scheduled start, which is tentatively for next Tuesday against the New York Mets. Gore has been up and down in 2026 in his first year with the Rangers, going into Wednesday's start with an 8-11 record, career-high 4.62 ERA (3.77 FIP), and 1.35 WHIP with 172 strikeouts and 66 walks in 161 2/3 innings across his 31 starts. He has not pitched into the sixth inning since his first start of the month on Sept. 1, and he has allowed at least three earned runs in each of his last three starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Dallas Morning News - Shawn McFarland
Sep 16, 2026, 11:10 PM ET
Updating a previous report, Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) said he felt his left groin "grab" during his pre-game bullpen, and he decided not to push it after the first inning on Wednesday in the 6-2 loss to the hosting Cincinnati Reds, according to Jack Harris of The California Post. Snell added that he will take things day to day, but he feels like he "should be good" to make another start before the end of the regular season. The Dodgers pulled the veteran southpaw after he threw a scoreless first inning with one hit allowed and a strikeout, but it sounds like he avoided a serious injury. The 33-year-old has a history of groin trouble, so although he might not think it is serious, the Dodgers could decide to play it safe and hold him out until the postseason in October. The 33-year-old two-time Cy Young winner has not been a picture of health in recent years and has only made 19 starts in the regular season for the Blue since joining them before the start of the 2025 season. Snell entered Wednesday's start with a nice 1.91 ERA, though, and he has also posted a 1.09 WHIP with 51 strikeouts and 16 walks in 37 2/3 innings across seven starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The California Post - Jack Harris
Nick Kurtz Begins Hitting Progression
                        
                            
                                Will Brady
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Athletics first baseman Nick Kurtz (thumb) has begun a hitting progression, per Martin Gallegos of MLB.com. Kurtz has been sidelined since late July by a right thumb strain and has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. Still, Gallegos reports that A's manager Mark Kotsay said the team is hoping Kurtz can progress to taking batting practice at some point in the next couple of weeks. Across 434 plate appearances before suffering the injury, the 23-year-old hit .256/.396/.483 with 21 home runs, 69 RBI, 62 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. Kurtz's batting average upside is limited by his elevated 32.5% strikeout rate, but he remains an OBP asset with his elite 18.2% walk rate. The lefty slugger also profiles as one of the best power hitters in baseball when healthy, posting an 18% barrel rate and a 57.3% hard-hit rate in 2026. Assuming Kurtz makes a full recovery over the offseason, he should come off the board in the first few rounds of fantasy drafts heading into 2027.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com - Martín Gallegos
Sep 16, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Atlanta Braves starting pitcher Chris Sale's next scheduled start is being pushed back, per Jesus Cano of The Athletic. Cano reports that the veteran left-hander is "not dealing with anything" and that there is "no need to panic." Still, it appears that Sale's next scheduled start will now be next Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds instead of this upcoming weekend against the Houston Astros. Sale has been one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2026, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.18 ERA, 0.99 WHIP, and 190 strikeouts across 157 innings (26 starts). He was effective in his most recent outing on September 11, allowing three earned runs while recording six strikeouts across seven innings pitched against the Philadelphia Phillies. Still, with the Braves locked into a playoff berth, it looks like the team is prioritizing having Sale as fresh as possible in October.--Will Brady
Source: The Athletic - Jesus Cano
Sep 16, 2026, 10:36 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals outfielder Joshua Baez (side) is considered day-to-day after exiting early from his team's loss to the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday with side tightness, per Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Baez was hitless in four at-bats before leaving the game. Across 108 plate appearances since making his MLB debut in mid-August, the 23-year-old is hitting .230/.278/.510 with seven home runs, 18 RBI, 18 runs scored, and two stolen bases. Baez hit 34 home runs across 410 plate appearances at Triple-A this season and has posted impressive barrel (12.5%) and hard-hit (48.4%) rates in the big leagues. However, he's also struck out in 30.6% of his plate appearances while logging just a 3.7% walk rate. If Baez ends up missing time, Cardinals outfielder Bryan Torres could be in line for an increase in at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Derrick Goold
Sep 16, 2026, 10:28 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles infielder Jackson Holliday (wrist) has been placed on the 10-day injured list due to left wrist inflammation. Infielder Jose Barrero was recalled from Triple-A Norfolk to take Holliday's place on the team's active roster. While Holliday could technically return to the Orioles before the end of the regular season, his 2026 campaign may be over. Across 354 plate appearances this year, the 22-year-old hit .229/.300/.340 with seven home runs, 30 RBI, 45 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. Holliday's season got off to a rough start, as he suffered a broken hamate bone in Spring Training that delayed his 2026 debut until mid-May. The young infielder has struck out in 23.7% of his plate appearances while also posting the worst hard-hit rate of his career (33.1%). With Holliday sidelined, Orioles infielder/outfielder Jeremiah Jackson will likely see an increase in playing time at second base.--Will Brady
Source: Baltimore Orioles
Sep 16, 2026, 10:17 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said that starting pitcher Kyle Bradish (abdomen) has been diagnosed with a sports hernia and is "going through the potential options," per Jake Rill of MLB.com. Bradish was placed on the 15-day injured list on Sunday, and his 2026 season is now almost certainly over. Across 155 innings (29 starts) before the hernia issue, Bradish recorded a 7-15 record with a 4.12 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, and 142 strikeouts. The 30-year-old's production faded in the second half, as he posted a 16.7% strikeout rate and a 5.29 ERA across 47 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. If Bradish has been pitching through discomfort over the last few months, it could explain the downturn in his numbers. Assuming he's ready to go for the start of the 2027 season, Bradish could be an under-the-radar bounce-back candidate for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com -Jake Rill
Sep 16, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) exited early from his start against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday due to groin tightness. The 33-year-old pitched a scoreless inning before leaving the game. Injuries have limited Snell to just 38 2/3 innings (eight starts) in 2026, as he's also battled elbow and shoulder ailments. The veteran has been highly effective when on the mound, pitching to a 1.86 ERA with four wins and 52 strikeouts. However, Snell has thrown just 100 total innings since the start of the 2024 season and may now be facing even more missed time. It's not yet clear whether Snell's groin injury will require another trip to the injured list, but the Dodgers will surely be cautious with him in order to try to have him on the mound in the postseason.--Will Brady
Source: Los Angeles Dodgers
Hunter Goodman Out Again With Thumb Injury
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 8:11 PM ET
Colorado Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman (thumb) remains sidelined for Wednesday's contest at Coors Field against the division-rival San Diego Padres, according to MLB.com. Braxton Fulford is doing the catching for right-hander Mason Adams and is hitting eighth against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray. Goodman is considered day-to-day with a thumb injury, but this will be his second straight missed game. The 26-year-old has missed three of the team's last four games, and with the Rockies having nothing left to play for, they are not going to put him in harm's way. The former fourth-rounder from the University of Memphis has become an elite power-hitting catcher over the last couple of seasons. Goodman has been an All-Star in each of the last two years while hitting a combined 69 home runs since the start of 2025. He currently sits with a .245/.312/.529 slash line, .841 OPS, a career-high 38 home runs, 81 RBI, 80 runs scored, and five stolen bases across his 129 games and 535 plate appearances. Check back to see if Goodman is good to go for Thursday's series finale against the Friars.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
CJ Abrams Returns to the Lineup Against Phillies
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 6:07 PM ET
Washington Nationals middle infielder CJ Abrams (neck) is starting at second base and will hit cleanup for the Nats on Wednesday at home against the division-rival Philadelphia Phillies and right-hander Zack Wheeler, per MLB.com. The Nationals scratched Abrams from Tuesday's win over Philly due to tightness in his neck, but he is back a day later and will be making just his sixth career start at the keystone as the team slowly transitions him from shortstop to second base to end the 2026 season. Fantasy managers will want to get Abrams back in their lineups immediately during his breakout season, in which he has hit .264/.339/.494 with an .834 OPS, 30 home runs, 96 RBI, 88 runs scored, and 29 stolen bases in 542 at-bats. The former first-rounder needs just one stolen base to join the elusive 30-30 club in his fifth year in the big leagues. Abrams is slowing down late in the year, though, hitting just .173 (17-for-98) in 24 games in August while going 10-for-44 (.227) with a homer, three doubles, four RBI, seven runs, three steals, four walks, and 14 strikeouts so far in 11 games in September. He has hit .296 with two RBI and a .914 OPS in 27 career at-bats against Wheeler.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Aaron Judge Leaves Wednesday's Game With Leg Tightness
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 5:22 PM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (leg) left Wednesday's game early against the Minnesota Twins in the top of the sixth inning with tightness in his lower right leg, according to Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. Before being replaced in right field by Heliot Ramos at Target Field, Judge went 0-for-2 at the plate with two strikeouts. The three-time MVP's early exit does not necessarily mean that he is dealing with a serious injury, as manager Aaron Boone could have pulled the All-Star slugger prematurely to give him more rest going into a scheduled off day after he has missed most of the 2026 season due to a stress fracture in his rib. Fantasy managers will be hoping that Judge can return for Friday's series opener in the desert against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Judge has struggled to find any consistency since his return from the IL, going just 4-for-21 (.190) with a homer, three RBI, two runs scored, one walk, and 11 strikeouts. The Yankees are playing for a postseason spot in the final week-plus of the season, but they also want their best power hitter as healthy as possible for October.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Brendan Kuty
Colson Montgomery Leaves Early With Wrist Contusion
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 3:33 PM ET
Chicago White Sox infielder Colson Montgomery (wrist) left Wednesday's game against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians with a left-wrist contusion, according to the team. Montgomery is being further evaluated after he was hit by a pitch in the fourth inning. In addition to being hit by a pitch, the 24-year-old left-handed slugger walked before being replaced at third base by Miguel Vargas, who moved over from first base. Munetaka Murakami entered the game to play first base. Montgomery, the 22nd overall pick in 2021, will likely undergo X-rays to rule out a fracture in his wrist. A significant injury at this point in the season could make Montgomery unavailable for the postseason next month, which would be a big loss for the Pale Hose. Montgomery came into Wednesday's contest hitting just over the Mendoza Line in his first full season in the majors, but he has also contributed 31 home runs and 84 RBI in his 144 games. The young infielder has 51 homers in his first 214 big-league games, making him a must-roster player for his power from the left side. If his injury is not serious, Montgomery could return as soon as Thursday's series opener against the division-rival Detroit Tigers.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Chicago White Sox
Sep 16, 2026, 3:05 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop prospect Emil Morales showed over the final month of the High-A season why he's one of the top offensive prospects in the Dodgers system, going 21-for-50 (.420) with four doubles, four home runs, two steals, and a 6:9 BB:K over a 12-game stretch before cooling off over the final three games (1-for-13). The Dodgers' fourth-ranked prospect began the year at Single-A and earned a promotion after 36 games, then went on to post a .281/.380/.534 slash line with 20 home runs in 81 games at High-A. The 6-foot-3 slugger has produced at every stop since entering professional baseball at the age of 17 in 2024, showing off his big power along the way, although he does have a propensity to strike out (25.6 percent K% in '26). So long as he keeps that under control, the native of Spain should continue to quickly climb the organizational ladder, with eyes potentially on a debut in 2028.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 16, 2026, 2:54 PM ET
Boston Red Sox infield prospect Franklin Arias has been on a tear at Triple-A Worcester of late, going 20-for-49 (.408) with four doubles, a home run, two steals, and a 5:4 BB:K over his last 11 games there. It has pushed his slash line to .331/.392/.503 with five home runs in 38 games at Triple-A, all while being one of only a handful of 20-year-olds who have performed at that level this season. Boston's top-ranked prospect has moved up all the way to the No. 3 prospect in all of baseball per MLB.com, and is showing that he's not overmatched there with just a 15.1 percent strikeout rate; as hot as he is, there's still a chance for a late-season cameo in the big leagues. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, the 5-foot-11 Venezuelan looks like he'll be in the mix for a starting role on the infield early next year, and with a strong blend of contact and power, he could quickly become fantasy-relevant. He should be stashed away already in dynasty leagues, but redraft managers had better familiarize themselves with the name.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Rainiel Rodriguez Keeps Rolling at Double-A
                        
                            
                                Jarod Rupp
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 2:44 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals catching prospect Rainiel Rodriguez picked up where he left off the regular season, collecting a pair of base hits in Double-A Springfield's 9-7 playoff win on Tuesday. The Cards' top-ranked prospect finished off the regular season on a tear, going 17-for-41 (.415) with four home runs and more walks (eight) than strikeouts (six) over his final 11 games. The Dominican backstop began the year at High-A, but seemingly got even better upon his promotion to Double-A, producing a .328/.408/.591 slash line with 23 home runs in 87 games for Springfield; he did all that as one of the few 19-year-olds at that level. The right-handed hitter should get a shot at Triple-A next season, and at that point, the talented youngster will be knocking on the door to the majors. His arrow is pointing way up in dynasty formats and should be stashed away as soon as possible if not already rostered.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Mathias LaCombe to be Promoted to Triple-A
                        
                            
                                Jarod Rupp
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 2:29 PM ET
Chicago White Sox pitching prospect Mathias LaCombe will be promoted to Triple-A Charlotte following a strong finish to the Double-A campaign. The right-hander recorded a 1.12 ERA, 0.75 WHIP, and an 18.5 percent K-BB% over his final 12 appearances (16 innings pitched) for Birmingham. Across 434 plate appearances before suffering the injury, the 23-year-old hit .256/.396/.483 with 21 home runs, 69 RBI, 62 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. Kurtz's batting average upside is limited by his elevated 32.5% strikeout rate, but he remains an OBP asset with his elite 18.2% walk rate. The lefty slugger also profiles as one of the best power hitters in baseball when healthy, posting an 18% barrel rate and a 57.3% hard-hit rate in 2026. Assuming Kurtz makes a full recovery over the offseason, he should come off the board in the first few rounds of fantasy drafts heading into 2027.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com - Martín Gallegos
Sep 16, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Atlanta Braves starting pitcher Chris Sale's next scheduled start is being pushed back, per Jesus Cano of The Athletic. Cano reports that the veteran left-hander is "not dealing with anything" and that there is "no need to panic." Still, it appears that Sale's next scheduled start will now be next Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds instead of this upcoming weekend against the Houston Astros. Sale has been one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2026, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.18 ERA, 0.99 WHIP, and 190 strikeouts across 157 innings (26 starts). He was effective in his most recent outing on September 11, allowing three earned runs while recording six strikeouts across seven innings pitched against the Philadelphia Phillies. Still, with the Braves locked into a playoff berth, it looks like the team is prioritizing having Sale as fresh as possible in October.--Will Brady
Source: The Athletic - Jesus Cano
Sep 16, 2026, 10:36 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals outfielder Joshua Baez (side) is considered day-to-day after exiting early from his team's loss to the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday with side tightness, per Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Baez was hitless in four at-bats before leaving the game. Across 108 plate appearances since making his MLB debut in mid-August, the 23-year-old is hitting .230/.278/.510 with seven home runs, 18 RBI, 18 runs scored, and two stolen bases. Baez hit 34 home runs across 410 plate appearances at Triple-A this season and has posted impressive barrel (12.5%) and hard-hit (48.4%) rates in the big leagues. However, he's also struck out in 30.6% of his plate appearances while logging just a 3.7% walk rate. If Baez ends up missing time, Cardinals outfielder Bryan Torres could be in line for an increase in at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Derrick Goold
Sep 16, 2026, 10:28 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles infielder Jackson Holliday (wrist) has been placed on the 10-day injured list due to left wrist inflammation. Infielder Jose Barrero was recalled from Triple-A Norfolk to take Holliday's place on the team's active roster. While Holliday could technically return to the Orioles before the end of the regular season, his 2026 campaign may be over. Across 354 plate appearances this year, the 22-year-old hit .229/.300/.340 with seven home runs, 30 RBI, 45 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. Holliday's season got off to a rough start, as he suffered a broken hamate bone in Spring Training that delayed his 2026 debut until mid-May. The young infielder has struck out in 23.7% of his plate appearances while also posting the worst hard-hit rate of his career (33.1%). With Holliday sidelined, Orioles infielder/outfielder Jeremiah Jackson will likely see an increase in playing time at second base.--Will Brady
Source: Baltimore Orioles
Sep 16, 2026, 10:17 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said that starting pitcher Kyle Bradish (abdomen) has been diagnosed with a sports hernia and is "going through the potential options," per Jake Rill of MLB.com. Bradish was placed on the 15-day injured list on Sunday, and his 2026 season is now almost certainly over. Across 155 innings (29 starts) before the hernia issue, Bradish recorded a 7-15 record with a 4.12 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, and 142 strikeouts. The 30-year-old's production faded in the second half, as he posted a 16.7% strikeout rate and a 5.29 ERA across 47 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. If Bradish has been pitching through discomfort over the last few months, it could explain the downturn in his numbers. Assuming he's ready to go for the start of the 2027 season, Bradish could be an under-the-radar bounce-back candidate for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com -Jake Rill
Sep 16, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) exited early from his start against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday due to groin tightness. The 33-year-old pitched a scoreless inning before leaving the game. Injuries have limited Snell to just 38 2/3 innings (eight starts) in 2026, as he's also battled elbow and shoulder ailments. The veteran has been highly effective when on the mound, pitching to a 1.86 ERA with four wins and 52 strikeouts. However, Snell has thrown just 100 total innings since the start of the 2024 season and may now be facing even more missed time. It's not yet clear whether Snell's groin injury will require another trip to the injured list, but the Dodgers will surely be cautious with him in order to try to have him on the mound in the postseason.--Will Brady
Source: Los Angeles Dodgers
Hunter Goodman Out Again With Thumb Injury
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 8:11 PM ET
Colorado Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman (thumb) remains sidelined for Wednesday's contest at Coors Field against the division-rival San Diego Padres, according to MLB.com. Braxton Fulford is doing the catching for right-hander Mason Adams and is hitting eighth against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray. Goodman is considered day-to-day with a thumb injury, but this will be his second straight missed game. The 26-year-old has missed three of the team's last four games, and with the Rockies having nothing left to play for, they are not going to put him in harm's way. The former fourth-rounder from the University of Memphis has become an elite power-hitting catcher over the last couple of seasons. Goodman has been an All-Star in each of the last two years while hitting a combined 69 home runs since the start of 2025. He currently sits with a .245/.312/.529 slash line, .841 OPS, a career-high 38 home runs, 81 RBI, 80 runs scored, and five stolen bases across his 129 games and 535 plate appearances. Check back to see if Goodman is good to go for Thursday's series finale against the Friars.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
CJ Abrams Returns to the Lineup Against Phillies
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 6:07 PM ET
Washington Nationals middle infielder CJ Abrams (neck) is starting at second base and will hit cleanup for the Nats on Wednesday at home against the division-rival Philadelphia Phillies and right-hander Zack Wheeler, per MLB.com. The Nationals scratched Abrams from Tuesday's win over Philly due to tightness in his neck, but he is back a day later and will be making just his sixth career start at the keystone as the team slowly transitions him from shortstop to second base to end the 2026 season. Fantasy managers will want to get Abrams back in their lineups immediately during his breakout season, in which he has hit .264/.339/.494 with an .834 OPS, 30 home runs, 96 RBI, 88 runs scored, and 29 stolen bases in 542 at-bats. The former first-rounder needs just one stolen base to join the elusive 30-30 club in his fifth year in the big leagues. Abrams is slowing down late in the year, though, hitting just .173 (17-for-98) in 24 games in August while going 10-for-44 (.227) with a homer, three doubles, four RBI, seven runs, three steals, four walks, and 14 strikeouts so far in 11 games in September. He has hit .296 with two RBI and a .914 OPS in 27 career at-bats against Wheeler.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Aaron Judge Leaves Wednesday's Game With Leg Tightness
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 5:22 PM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (leg) left Wednesday's game early against the Minnesota Twins in the top of the sixth inning with tightness in his lower right leg, according to Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. Before being replaced in right field by Heliot Ramos at Target Field, Judge went 0-for-2 at the plate with two strikeouts. The three-time MVP's early exit does not necessarily mean that he is dealing with a serious injury, as manager Aaron Boone could have pulled the All-Star slugger prematurely to give him more rest going into a scheduled off day after he has missed most of the 2026 season due to a stress fracture in his rib. The Yankees are playing for a postseason spot in the final week-plus of the season, but they also want their best power hitter as healthy as possible for October.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Brendan Kuty
Colson Montgomery Leaves Early With Wrist Contusion
                        
                            
                                Keith Hernandez
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 3:33 PM ET
Chicago White Sox infielder Colson Montgomery (wrist) left Wednesday's game against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians with a left-wrist contusion, according to the team. Montgomery is being further evaluated after he was hit by a pitch in the fourth inning. In addition to being hit by a pitch, the 24-year-old left-handed slugger walked before being replaced at third base by Miguel Vargas, who moved over from first base. Munetaka Murakami entered the game to play first base. Montgomery, the 22nd overall pick in 2021, will likely undergo X-rays to rule out a fracture in his wrist. A significant injury at this point in the season could make Montgomery unavailable for the postseason next month, which would be a big loss for the Pale Hose. Montgomery came into Wednesday's contest hitting just over the Mendoza Line in his first full season in the majors, but he has also contributed 31 home runs and 84 RBI in his 144 games. The young infielder has 51 homers in his first 214 big-league games, making him a must-roster player for his power from the left side. If his injury is not serious, Montgomery could return as soon as Thursday's series opener against the division-rival Detroit Tigers.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Chicago White Sox
Sep 16, 2026, 3:05 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop prospect Emil Morales showed over the final month of the High-A season why he's one of the top offensive prospects in the Dodgers system, going 21-for-50 (.420) with four doubles, four home runs, two steals, and a 6:9 BB:K over a 12-game stretch before cooling off over the final three games (1-for-13). The Dodgers' fourth-ranked prospect began the year at Single-A and earned a promotion after 36 games, then went on to post a .281/.380/.534 slash line with 20 home runs in 81 games at High-A. The 6-foot-3 slugger has produced at every stop since entering professional baseball at the age of 17 in 2024, showing off his big power along the way, although he does have a propensity to strike out (25.6 percent K% in '26). So long as he keeps that under control, the native of Spain should continue to quickly climb the organizational ladder, with eyes potentially on a debut in 2028.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 16, 2026, 2:54 PM ET
Boston Red Sox infield prospect Franklin Arias has been on a tear at Triple-A Worcester of late, going 20-for-49 (.408) with four doubles, a home run, two steals, and a 5:4 BB:K over his last 11 games there. It has pushed his slash line to .331/.392/.503 with five home runs in 38 games at Triple-A, all while being one of only a handful of 20-year-olds who have performed at that level this season. Boston's top-ranked prospect has moved up all the way to the No. 3 prospect in all of baseball per MLB.com, and is showing that he's not overmatched there with just a 15.1 percent strikeout rate; as hot as he is, there's still a chance for a late-season cameo in the big leagues. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, the 5-foot-11 Venezuelan looks like he'll be in the mix for a starting role on the infield early next year, and with a strong blend of contact and power, he could quickly become fantasy-relevant. He should be stashed away already in dynasty leagues, but redraft managers had better familiarize themselves with the name.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Rainiel Rodriguez Keeps Rolling at Double-A
                        
                            
                                Jarod Rupp
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 2:44 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals catching prospect Rainiel Rodriguez picked up where he left off the regular season, collecting a pair of base hits in Double-A Springfield's 9-7 playoff win on Tuesday. The Cards' top-ranked prospect finished off the regular season on a tear, going 17-for-41 (.415) with four home runs and more walks (eight) than strikeouts (six) over his final 11 games. The Dominican backstop began the year at High-A, but seemingly got even better upon his promotion to Double-A, producing a .328/.408/.591 slash line with 23 home runs in 87 games for Springfield; he did all that as one of the few 19-year-olds at that level. The right-handed hitter should get a shot at Triple-A next season, and at that point, the talented youngster will be knocking on the door to the majors. His arrow is pointing way up in dynasty formats and should be stashed away as soon as possible if not already rostered.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com

                    Sep 16, 2026, 2:29 PM ET

Source: MiLB Central

                                Jarod Rupp
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 16, 2026, 2:20 PM ET
